REPORTER'S TRANSCRIPT — Motion to Suppress Hearing (Excerpts)
People v. Barrett, CR-2023-04418
Date: November 9, 2023
Before: Hon. D. Sutter
Reporter: K. Onuoha, CSR #18874

[RT 78]
DIRECT EXAMINATION OF TROOPER J. REEVES, by ADA M. Powell:

Q: Trooper, what information did you receive on May 18?
A: A tip came in through our online portal. It said a Black male in his late twenties was driving a silver SUV in the Marion area and had drugs in the car.

Q: Did the tip provide any additional information?
A: No. No name, no plate, no specific location, no time. Just that description.

Q: Was the tip anonymous?
A: Yes.

Q: Was there any indication of how the tipster came by this information?
A: No.

Q: Had this tipster ever provided information before?
A: There's no way to know — it was anonymous through the portal.

[RT 94]
CROSS-EXAMINATION, by DEFENSE COUNSEL A. MERCER:

Q: Trooper, before you stopped Mr. Barrett's vehicle, did you observe any traffic violation?
A: No, sir.

Q: Erratic driving?
A: No.

Q: Anything suspicious about the manner of operation?
A: No.

Q: The basis for the stop was solely the tip?
A: Yes.

Q: How long did you follow Mr. Barrett before stopping him?
A: Around 2 miles. 2.4 miles, my report says.

Q: Did you call for backup or for a K-9 unit before stopping?
A: No.

Q: After you stopped him, did you request consent to search?
A: No, I didn't request consent.

Q: Did you have a warrant?
A: No.

Q: You searched the vehicle anyway?
A: Yes, based on the tip and what I saw.

Q: What did you see?
A: He seemed nervous.

[RT 142–198 omitted: trial court ruling denying suppression motion]

[RT 211]
MOTION IN LIMINE HEARING:

[RT 218] DEFENSE COUNSEL: ... Mr. Barrett's exact words on the recording at 02:14:08 of the interrogation video are, quote, "I want a lawyer for the questions about the drugs in my car." That's an unequivocal invocation under Edwards.

[RT 220] ADA POWELL: Your Honor, the invocation was limited in scope by the defendant himself. The questions that followed concerned an entirely different incident from 2021 — not "the drugs in his car."

[RT 224] THE COURT: I'll allow it. The invocation as phrased was limited to the immediate charge. The State's questions about the 2021 incident fall outside that scope.

[RT 228] DEFENSE COUNSEL: Objection preserved.
